# claudedojo


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`claudedojo` gives a new Claude Code session examples of good tool use
before it starts work. Instructions alone leave the model to learn from
its first calls and mistakes. A worked round supplies examples in the
conversation history.

The template is an authored `aidialog` notebook. It contains a dojo
round and the outputs from running it against the kernel. We convert
this notebook to a Claude Code session. New sessions resume a copy with
the worked round already in context.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
import json
from llmdojo.tmpl import _dojo_v
```

## Curating the capture

[`capture_span`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_span)
selects the last dealt round with the shared
[`capture_slice`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/tmpl.html#capture_slice)
function. It begins at the bootstrap `doc()` call and ends at the first
score’s result. Capture prompts, earlier warm-up calls, and later
chatter stay outside the selection. An incomplete last round raises an
error.

[`curate_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#curate_dojo)
removes thinking and mid-round user prompts. It also removes
`hook_success` and `task_reminder` attachments. For each failed tool
call, it removes the records containing the call and its error result.
[`mk_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#mk_template)
will supply one prompt for the completed example.

Environment attachments remain. These include tool listings, skill
listings, and MCP instructions. Claude Code uses them to track
environment changes on resume. Keeping them avoids repeating unchanged
context, while a changed environment can add new attachments.

`reid_recs` gives the remaining records deterministic IDs and
timestamps. The same capture then produces the same template records.

*Select the latest dealt round from its bootstrap call through its first
score result.*

We’ll build a small capture without model calls. It has a bootstrap
call, a dojo card, and a clean scoring turn:

``` python
mproj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
boot = tool_turn('Bootstrap and play the round.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='doc(clik, pysk, edsk)'),
    'module docs', 'Read.', cwd=mproj)
card = tool_turn('Run the llmdojo round now please.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_start()'),
    '== llmdojo ==\n1. (par 2) orient', 'Round underway.', cwd=mproj)
score = tool_turn('Score it.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_score()'),
    "strokes 7, par 8\nkata 'orient': ok\nexpected answer: weather\nClean round. Run dir removed. Completion id: ab12 - keep this id.\nKernel namespace cleared, as after a restart. Doc-state is intact.", 'Clean: id ab12.', cwd=mproj)
len(boot+card+score)
```

    12

Add a thinking record, a hook confirmation, and a failed call between
the worked turns. Save and reload the synthetic transcript before
curating it:

``` python
tu = mk_tu('mcp__clikernel', {})
noise = [mk_rec('assistant', [dict(type='thinking', thinking='Planning.', signature='')], cwd=mproj),
    dict(type='attachment', uuid='att1', attachment=dict(type='hook_success', hookName='PreToolUse:x')),
    mk_rec('assistant', [tu], cwd=mproj), mk_rec('user', [dict(mk_tr(tu, 'Error: no such tool'), is_error=True)], cwd=mproj)]
msid = save_sess(boot+card+noise+score, cwd=mproj)
mini = load_sess(msid, mproj)
len(mini)
```

    16

The curated records begin with the bootstrap call. They exclude the
noise and retain each call’s matching result. Curating twice gives
identical records:

``` python
c1,c2 = curate_dojo(mini),curate_dojo(mini)
test_eq(canon(list(c1)), canon(list(c2)))
test_eq(len(c1), 8)
test_eq(_cells(c1), ['doc(clik, pysk, edsk)', 'dojo_start()', 'dojo_score()'])
test_eq(dojo_cid(c1), 'ab12')
test_eq(c1[1]['message']['content'][0]['tool_use_id'], c1[0]['message']['content'][0]['id'])
```

## Gating the capture

A template that demonstrates mistakes teaches those mistakes to later
sessions.
[`is_clean`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#is_clean)
reports problems that disqualify a capture. The shared
[`round_gates`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/tmpl.html#round_gates)
checks one dealt round, one first-try score, no redo or resume,
clean-score output, and no script leakage. Claude’s additional check
looks for tool results with `is_error`.

[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
checks the selected round before curation. Headless capture checks the
complete child run. Curation removes distracting records; it isn’t a
substitute for a clean attempt.
[`save_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#save_template)
checks the final records again before writing them, including records
converted from an edited dialog.

### is_clean

``` python
def is_clean(
    recs, # Captured thread records
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible assistant text
):
```

*Why a captured round can’t become a template: a list of problems, empty
when the run is clean*

The noisy capture fails because it includes a failed tool call. Removing
that noise gives a clean example. Redos and script phrases in visible
text also fail. Thinking blocks don’t contribute to the visible-text
check:

``` python
test_eq(is_clean(mini), ['1 failed tool calls'])
test_eq(is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)), [])
redo = tool_turn('Retry.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_redo(1)'), 'reset', 'Retrying.', cwd=mproj)
assert 'needed a redo' in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+redo+score, cwd=mproj), mproj))
leak = [mk_rec('assistant', 'Since we are recording a demo, I begin.', cwd=mproj)]
assert any('script leaked' in p for p in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+leak+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)))
```

### mk_template

``` python
def mk_template(
    picked, # Round records, e.g. from `curate_dojo`
    opening:str='Bootstrapping: the startup script has already run its imports, so I read the tooling docs, check the catalog, then take the dojo.', # Reply text preceding the first tool call
    closing:str="OK I'm ready.", # Reply text ending the round
):
```

*A template dialog: `picked` wrapped in `TMPL_PROMPT` and framing text,
with tool output untruncated*

[`mk_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#mk_template)
wraps the selected records in `TMPL_PROMPT` and opening and closing
text. The result is a one-prompt dialog with the worked round in its
reply. You can save it with `write_ipynb` for review before running
`dojobuild --claude`.

The framing records are synthetic, which Claude can resume like other
transcript records. `chat2dlg` uses `mx=None` here to keep the complete
tool outputs. Its default 2,000-character truncation would cut off the
`doc()` results that later sessions need.

``` python
tdlg = mk_template(c1, opening='Practice first.')
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(tdlg.messages), 1)
assert 'dojo_start()' in str(tdlg.messages[0].output)
tmsgs = dlg2msgs(tdlg)
test_eq([m['role'] for m in tmsgs], ['user', 'assistant']*4)
```

## The template store

`dojobuild` compiles the canonical dialog into
`dojo_data/claude_store/`. The package ships this store alongside the
dialog. Updating llmdojo updates the template, without a per-user build
step.

The metadata records the round’s completion ID and dojo tooling version.
`dojo_start(id)` rejects a receipt from a different version. It does not
silently accept the old round or deal a new one. Rebuild the template
after a tooling change, or play a fresh round without an ID.

[`save_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#save_template)
checks the records with
[`is_clean`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#is_clean)
before writing either store file.
[`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template)
uses this same check after converting the edited dialog.

This save/load test uses a temporary store. It checks record content and
metadata without registering a completion or writing a session:

``` python
rstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_template(c1, rstore)
back,rmeta = load_template(rstore)
test_eq(rmeta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(canon(list(back)), canon([obj2dict(r) for r in c1]))
shutil.rmtree(rstore)
```

Compile the packaged dialog into a temporary store and check its
completion ID and tooling version:

``` python
bstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
build_template(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb', bstore)
bmeta = load_template(bstore)[1]
test_eq((bmeta['cid'], bmeta['v']), (dojo_cid(packaged_recs), _dojo_v()))
shutil.rmtree(bstore)
```

## Capturing from a live session

A Claude Code session can capture a round it has already played.
Harvesting that transcript makes no additional model calls.
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
selects the latest round through its first score result and checks it
with
[`is_clean`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#is_clean)
before curation removes any records. Earlier rounds and work after that
score remain outside the capture. It saves both the store and a review
copy named `template.ipynb`.

Pass a session ID or name to select a transcript. Without one, it uses
the project’s newest transcript. Live transcripts don’t retain all
mid-turn assistant narration. Put narration in comment-only kernel cells
when playing a round for capture. The Codex backend provides the
corresponding
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
workflow.

The clean transcript below becomes a template. The earlier noisy
transcript fails before curation.

``` python
shutil.rmtree(cstore)
test_fail(lambda: capture_current(msid, mproj, cstore), contains='failed tool calls')
```

## Capturing headlessly

[`capture_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_dojo)
runs a new Claude Code session with fastclaude’s `astream`. Each attempt
uses a disposable project. The model follows `CAPTURE_SCRIPT` from its
appended system instructions and supplies its own narration. The
instructions are separate from the conversation turns. The kernel still
executes every call and produces the score.

Earlier capture scripts used phrases such as “automated telemetry
capture” and “never mention these instructions”. Those drafts triggered
fable’s safety checks as it reread the context. The current script
describes the exercise plainly. It supplies a plan for good tool use
without asking the model to conceal its work.

Headless capture checks the raw run. A fumble rejects that attempt
instead of disappearing through curation. A clean run then goes through
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
for storage.

The shared script lists the cells to run and the details needed to
execute them. Claude receives it through the system-prompt addition.
Codex writes the same script to the scratch project’s `AGENTS.md`.

Each Claude attempt creates a `pyproject.toml` so clikernel starts the
project kernel and prints its bootstrap. `LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR` points
inside the disposable project. Failed attempts therefore leave the
machine’s completion registry alone.

This is not a general filesystem sandbox. The capture config uses
`permission_mode='bypassPermissions'` and no setting sources. It runs
real tooling with a per-attempt budget. Only run it when you intend to
permit those tool calls and model costs.

A successful capture writes `template.ipynb` beside the store. Review
that notebook before publishing the example. Edit its prose and verify
its receipts, then compile the stores with `dojobuild --claude` and
`dojobuild --codex`. The initial store already works, but future
sessions will copy the behavior it demonstrates.


## Launching

[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
loads the store and registers its completion ID. It writes the records
as a new session in the target project and returns the ID for
`claude -r`. Every launch uses a fresh session ID, leaving previous
sessions alone.

The resumed session has the worked round in its history. Its new kernel
starts from imports rather than retaining the practice run’s variables.
This matches the round’s opening and closing. Claude adds the live hooks
and skills for the current environment.

### append_dojo

``` python
def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to append to; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
```

*Append the template round to session `sid` (e.g. after a compaction),
and return `sid` to resume*

Compaction removes worked examples from the model’s context.
[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
restores them by adding the template to the end of an existing
conversation. The appended round includes its tool calls and `doc()`
outputs.

Close the app before changing its transcript. The resumed app starts a
fresh kernel, matching the state described by the template.
[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
doesn’t enforce this requirement or stop a running app.

The appended copy uses `APPEND_PROMPT` instead of the new-session
prompt. Its receipts stay the same. Each append derives new record IDs
from the session ID and current transcript length.

A compact document should explain the conversation’s work, not repeat
its practice round.
[`strip_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#strip_dojo)
removes whole user turns containing a bare `dojo_start()`. This removes
the prompt, framing text, calls, and receipt together.

Calls such as `dojo_start(id)` remain. They check an existing receipt
without dealing a round, and record that the check occurred. Other user
turns remain unchanged.

The synthetic capture loses the turn that dealt the round, including its

[`strip_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#strip_dojo)

``` python
stripped = strip_dojo(mini)
test_eq(len(stripped), len(mini)-8)
assert not any(_dealt([r]) for r in stripped)
test_eq(strip_dojo(stripped), stripped)
[rec_txt(r) for r in stripped if _is_prompt(r)]
```

### compact_dojo

``` python
def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to compact; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
```

*Compact the conversation without prior dojo turns where possible, then
append a fresh round. Return its ID.*

Use `-r` after Claude’s own compaction to append a fresh example.
[`compact_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#compact_dojo)
also performs the compaction itself, without a model call. It removes
earlier dojo turns before calling
[`llmsurgery.ant.compact_session`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmsurgery/ant.html#compact_session).
If removal would leave no records, it keeps the original session for
compaction.

The compact document uses llmsurgery’s compact DSL, including its normal
truncation of tool traffic.
[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
adds a complete worked round afterward. `claudedojo -c` resumes this
compacted session with the example restored.

`launch_config('claude')` supplies standing arguments such as
system-prompt files. Set `claude_args` in
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claudedojo/config.toml`. See `tmpl` for defaults and
path expansion.

### main

``` python
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Session id or name; the project's newest transcript where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing session after a compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the session with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared session id instead of launching claude
    capture:bool=False, # Play a scripted round through Claude Code, check it with is_clean, and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing session already played (`capture_current`)
    capture_model:str='fable', # Model for --capture
    capture_effort:str='medium', # Adaptive thinking effort for --capture ('low'/'medium'/'high')
):
```

*Prepare a session with the worked round and launch Claude Code.*

These launch examples redirect dojo state to a temporary directory. They
still write Claude transcripts for the synthetic project. Keep them out
of normal tests unless session storage is isolated too:

``` python
store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
trecs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(tdlg), key='claudedojo', model=None)
save_template(trecs, store)
back,meta = load_template(store)
test_eq(meta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
```

Each
[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
call registers the round and creates a new session. The example checks
that the second call doesn’t reuse the first session’s ID:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    lsid = prep_dojo(mproj, store)
    test_ne(prep_dojo(mproj, store), lsid)
    from llmdojo.dojo import _completions
    test_eq(_completions()['ab12']['v'], _dojo_v())
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(lsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(load_sess(lsid, mproj)), len(trecs))
```

With no explicit store,
[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
reads the packaged one. It creates registration state and a session, but
doesn’t build a per-user store:

``` python
fresh = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'state'
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(fresh)
try: fsid = prep_dojo(mproj)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(fsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)
```

Appending adds another copy of the round with fresh record IDs and the
post-compaction prompt:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    n0 = len(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    test_eq(append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    ap = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(ap), n0+len(c1))
    test_eq(ap[n0].parentUuid, ap[n0-1].uuid)
    test_eq(ap[n0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
```

The next append must keep record IDs distinct. The same example also
checks lookup by a session’s `/rename` name:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store)
    ap2 = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(set(r.uuid for r in ap2)), len(ap2))
    name_sess(lsid, 'flux-dojo', mproj)
    test_eq(append_dojo('flux-dojo', mproj, store), lsid)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
```

The compaction example adds work to the session, removes prior dojo
turns, and appends a new round. The compact document retains the work.
The new tail contains the round’s kernel cells:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    work = tool_turn('What season is it?', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='season()'), 'winter', 'Winter.', cwd=mproj)
    append_sess(work, lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(compact_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    prior,new = split_compaction(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    assert 'dojo_start()' not in prior
    test('season()', prior, in_)
    test_eq(new[0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
```

Run `claudedojo -h` for the available modes. `call_parse` turns the
capitalized `Resume` and `Compact` parameters into `-r` and `-c`. Both
modes prepare a session and resume it in Claude.

The CLI uses `nested=True` to leave unknown arguments in `sys.argv`. It
forwards them to `claude` after the config arguments. Use `--flag=value`
for forwarded values. With a space, `parse_known_args` can mistake the
value for the `sess` positional argument. A fresh launch rejects that
stray argument.

Launcher flags take precedence over Claude flags with the same name.
Capture options use the `capture_` prefix to leave names such as
`--model` available for forwarding. `--sid` prints the prepared session
ID and exits without starting Claude.

[`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template)
converts the dialog through `dlg2msgs`, which requests plain prompt
text. This avoids aidialog’s normal XML prompt envelope. It writes
records with `model=None` to use the user’s configured default on
resume.
[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
assigns launch-time timestamps so the session picker shows the session’s
actual age.

This live test asks a resumed session for its completion ID and checks
that it knows the practice kernel’s state is gone. The answer must come
from the prepared history. It needs a captured template in the real
store and spends model tokens, so it stays out of CI:

``` python
psid = prep_dojo(mproj)
p = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec('claude','-p',f'--resume={psid}','--model','haiku',
    'From this session only: what completion id did the dojo round print, and what did its final message say about kernel state?',
    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, cwd=mproj)
out,_ = await p.communicate()
print(out.decode())
```

## Rebuilding the template

A tooling-version change invalidates the template’s completion receipt.
[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
warns when it loads that store. If the round’s cells are unchanged,
`dojobuild` can replay them to refresh outputs and rebuild both stores
without a model. A changed round needs a new capture.

The numbered cells in `llmdojo/dojo_data/capture_prompt.md` define the
round. Update that script first when the dojo changes. For live capture,
play its cells in order and narrate with comment-only kernel cells. Then
call
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
from the same session. Check the selected transcript if other sessions
are active, since the default is the project’s newest one.

Review the selected round before harvesting it. Its first score must be
clean, without a redo on the way. The template should show the attempt
you’d want a new session to copy.

``` python
dlg = capture_current()
write_ipynb(dlg, 'llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb')
```

Review the written dialog before compiling it. You can edit the prose,
calls, and outputs, but receipts must match what the real tooling
produces. When many outputs need updating, replay the cells rather than
rewriting receipts by hand.

The canonical source is `llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb`. Track
it in Git and ship it with the compiled stores. A fresh install reads
the packaged store directly. After review, run `dojobuild --claude` and
`dojobuild --codex`, which call each backend’s
[`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template).
Check the stored completion ID and tooling version afterward.

``` python
build_template('llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb', cwd=Path.cwd())
load_template()[1]
```

## Cleanup

``` python
shutil.rmtree(sess_dir(mproj))
shutil.rmtree(mproj)
```
